incentives.name: Class seventeen property: reduced property tax rate for qualified data centers
incentives.what: Land, buildings, equipment and supplies of a qualified data center are taxed at 0.9% of market value. Qualified: at least 300,000 sq ft and $150M total cost with construction after 2017-06-30, or 25,000 sq ft new/expanded and $50M within 48 months with construction after 2019-01-01. Includes cooling, substations, backup power, and (since 2025) on-site generation and storage that start after 2025-05-13 and are used at least 80% on site; dedicated communications lines and on-site generation get the rate for 10 years. Locally assessed; property in urban renewal or targeted economic development districts still pays school and state equalization mills. Montana has no general sales tax.

dockets.what: Petition by nine groups (MEIC, Montana PIRG, NW Energy Coalition, Climate Smart Missoula, Honor the Earth and others) asking the PSC to create a separate data center customer class and tariff and to require notice of data center load changes; NorthWestern says it will file a large-load tariff and submit data center contracts as executed (letters of intent for about 1,400 MW by 2030)

Application for a Large New Load tariff rule (LNL Rule) for new or expanded loads of 5 MW or more, including data centers; executed Electric Service Agreements of 50 MW or more would be filed for PSC approval before service. NorthWestern has development agreements with Sabey and Atlas Power and (April 2026) Quantica: 150 MW from late 2027, growing to about 1,500 MW or more by 2030. Docket number not found.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 265 (2025), Financial Freedom and Innovation Act
laws_and_bills.what: Revises cryptocurrency laws (session law chapter 379, 2025). Content not read; listed because it may cover crypto mining.

laws_and_bills.name: 2027 session bill drafts on data centers (LC0020, LC0022, LC0031, LC0058, LC0071, LC0181, LC0182, LC0235, LC0250, LC0251, LC0252, LC0253, LC0285)
laws_and_bills.what: Draft requests at 'drafter assigned' stage: generally revise data center laws; data center taxation (LC0022) and property taxation of data centers (LC0058); prohibit data centers in tax increment financing areas (LC0235); development laws (LC0250); protect ratepayers and fiscal protection (LC0251); transparency and accountability (LC0252); water use (LC0253); protect utility ratepayers from data center costs (LC0285).

laws_and_bills.name: Energy and Technology Interim Committee bill draft on large-load cost allocation
laws_and_bills.what: Committee requested a draft directing the PSC to regulate utilities so residential and small business customers don't pay for power serving large-load customers such as data centers.

local_rules.what: 2021 data center regulations: limited to industrial zones, special exception near homes, e-waste recycling verification, new renewable energy required

Interim zoning: temporary moratorium on new or expanded data centers countywide (zoned and unzoned areas, not inside Missoula city limits), unanimous; up to one year, extendable one year; county must start a study within 30 days. Prompted by the Krambu Bonner proposal (which is not covered because its application was already in).

local_rules.place: Fort Peck Indian Reservation (Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes)
local_rules.what: Tribal Executive Board voted to ban all future discussions with anyone proposing data centers on the reservation; three unnamed companies had approached the tribes.

Citizen initiative (406 People First) requiring voter approval of data center development. District court rejected it after a county-caused signature deadline error; Montana Supreme Court put it on the ballot Sept 22, 2026, then vacated that order Sept 24 because ballots were already mailed. Appeal pending; nonprofit sued the county in August.

Citizen initiative giving voters a say over data centers (prompted by Quantica's Broadview campus); organizers gathered 14,980 of 16,560 signatures before a judge ruled the deadline (July 13 under a 2025 state law) had passed; commissioners took no action Aug 18, 2026 and were to consider interim zoning.

polls.who: Montana Free Press - Rutgers Eagleton poll (registered voters, Aug 27 - Sept 7, 2026, +/-4.2%)
polls.what: Support for data centers in your city or a neighboring county
polls.result: Nearly 75% oppose; majority opposed in every party; 92% want state rules to limit data centers' impact on electricity prices; 45% say they create jobs vs 49% disagree.
